claims.text: Degradation of additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 during elevated-temperature exposure is primarily governed by selective oxidation of Al and Cr.
Al and Cr form a thin, adherent mixed oxide scale under oxidizing conditions.
The mixed Al/Cr oxide scale preserves the integrity of the fcc matrix.
Under reducing conditions, the protective mixed oxide scale is not sustained or is destabilized.
Loss or destabilization of the scale under reducing conditions enhances substrate degradation.
The additively manufactured starting alloy has a fully retained fcc matrix.
The starting alloy has an as-printed microstructure.
Under oxidizing conditions, Al and Cr preferentially oxidize relative to the other alloy constituents.
The fine, adherent mixed oxide scale limits further oxygen ingress.
Absence or destabilization of the protective oxide under reducing conditions can produce non-protective or discontinuous oxide layers.
Oxidizing exposure will produce a modest weight gain.
Oxidizing exposure will produce a uniform, adherent oxide scale.
The oxide scale formed in an oxidizing atmosphere will preserve the alloy's microstructural integrity.
Reducing exposure will inhibit protective-scale formation.
Reducing exposure will cause altered scale morphology or greater core-alloy degradation, including a higher degradation rate and microstructural damage.
The as-fabricated baseline has no pre-existing oxide scale or degradation features.
The proposed mechanism applies at approximately 800–1000°C in strongly oxidizing or reducing gases.
Changes in temperature, exposure time, or gas purity may activate overlapping or alternative degradation mechanisms.
